Definition: from G473 and the middle voice of G2192; to hold oneself opposite to, i.e. (by implication) adhere to; by extension to care for:--hold fast, hold to, support.
BiblicalUsage: To hold fast to the faithful word, to cleave to a master and despise the other. Jesus says no man can serve two masters, for he will hold to the one and despise the other, and Paul tells Titus to hold fast the faithful word so he can exhort and convince the gainsayers. The word is a grip that will not let go.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe holding fast is the whole of faithfulness in one grip: you cannot serve two masters, so you hold to one and let the other go. Paul's charge to Titus is my charge too, to hold the faithful word tight enough to teach it and defend it. I hold that the hand that grips Christ will not be shaken loose.
